messages:
zoe-sales: Quick update — BankGamma wants a Private deployment POC behind their SD-WAN. Requirements: literal client IP in our access logs, a single static egress IP for their firewall allowlist, and compatibility with their inline TLS-inspect appliance. They attached a SOC2 questionnaire link. Can eng advise a minimal topology and checklist?
alan-net: Short options: 1) PrivateLink (interface endpoint) + customer-side egress proxy that NATs to one IP and emits signed original-IP header 2) Routed VPC peering / Transit (preserves L3 source IP) 3) Connector appliance inside customer DMZ that forwards flows untouched. Tradeoffs: routing complexity vs operational surface.
priya-se: PrivateLink keeps customer changes minimal. If BankGamma insists on network-layer src IP, peering is the only way to preserve it end-to-end. Otherwise app-layer header with signature is commonly acceptable to auditors.
marta-arch: Header signing design: proxy adds X-Client-IP and X-Client-IP-Sig (HMAC-SHA256). Our ingress validates the signature, rejects mismatches, and records the original header and verification result to immutable audit logs. This gives tamper-evidence without full routing changes.
security-bot: Security guidance: E2E TLS to Redwood strongly preferred. If TLS inspection occurs, customer must provide documented key custody & rotation. Header-signature approach ok if signing keys are managed in customer's KMS and rotated per agreement. No header may be used as an authentication mechanism unless contractually approved.
zoe-sales: BankGamma says literal src IP is a "hard" audit requirement. They may accept signed headers only if Redwood provides a cryptographic attestation that verifies and logs the signature. Can we deliver such an attestation?
scott-pricing: Connector/appliance in-customer VPC is a billable add-on: onboarding fee + monthly infra + egress GB. PrivateLink-only POC is cheaper. I'll pull numbers from pricing ops and share a ballpark.
alan-net: Ops notes: watch MTU/MSS when crossing SD-WAN or IPSec; streaming sessions need NAT timeouts tuned; expose health endpoint on proxy (http 8081) so our monitors can verify liveness. Also include source port preservation caveats for UDP flows.
priya-se: Pasteable firewall allowlist sample (public-egress path):
`````
- 203.0.113.10/32 TCP 443 (redwood-ingress-1)
- 203.0.113.11/32 TCP 443 (redwood-ingress-2)
- NTP: UDP 123 to corporate NTP
- DNS: TCP/UDP 53 to corporate resolver
`````
If using PrivateLink: instead allow the proxy host to reach the interface ENIs/security-group recommended by our onboarding doc.
zoe-sales: Request from customer: can Redwood sign/issue an attestation stating we verify the HMAC and retain immutable logs for 90 days during the POC?
marta-arch: We can provide a scoped attestation for the POC period: "Redwood verifies X-Client-IP-Sig (HMAC-SHA256) and persists headers and verification outcome to immutable audit logs for the POC window." Legal/security to finalize language and include key handling constraints.
security-bot: Add to attestation pre-reqs: customer must confirm TLS-inspect operator has no access to the signing KMS keys and provide rotation cadence.
zoe-sales: Timeline: customer wants to start connectivity tests Friday. Can we produce checklist, diagram, and a small config snippet by EOD tomorrow?
alan-net: I'll draft the connectivity checklist + topology diagram (PrivateLink+proxy vs peering).
priya-se: I'll produce proxy container spec (image + env vars), sample iptables rules, and HMAC verification pseudocode.
scott-pricing: I'll deliver a 30-day POC quote and cost delta between PrivateLink-only and connector option by EOD.
zoe-sales: Great — thanks team :rocket: 
ops-bot: Reminder: ticket POC-998 created and assigned to eng-oncall for network onboarding.
